deep.reconstruction:
The page has no derivation. It is a combinatorial enumeration of arrangements of four letters a, b, c, d in four columns. Each column is a different way of ordering or grouping the four letters.

Column 1 lists linear permutations (type 1+1+1+1) in lexicographic order. After a false start (abcd, then acbd struck out), it restarts: abcd, abdc, acbd, acdb, adbc, adcb (all 6 beginning with a), then bacd, badc, bcad, bcda, bdac, bdca (all 6 beginning with b). That is 12 of the 4! = 24 permutations, exactly those with first letter a or b. The lists for c and d are not written out, so this is half the full list, presumably either abandoned or meant to be completed by symmetry (my inference).

Column 2 lists arrangements of the form x . yz . w, where yz is an unordered pair. I read these as ordered groupings of type 1+2+1:
- a.bc.d, a.bd.c, a.cd.b give the 3 choices of pair from {b,c,d} when a is first.
- b.ac.d, b.ad.c, b.dc.a give the 3 choices of pair from {a,c,d} when b is first.
- In b.dc.a the pair is written dc instead of cd. As an unordered pair this is equivalent.
The full count is 4·3 = 12 = 4!/2!. Again only the half with first element a or b is written, which parallels column 1.

Column 3 lists one singleton followed by the complementary triple (type 1+3): a.bcd, b.acd, c.abd, d.abc. This is all 4 = C(4,1) cases.

Column 4 lists ordered splittings into two pairs (type 2+2): ab cd, ac bd, ad bc, bc ad, bd ac, cd ab. This is all 6 = 4!/(2!2!) ordered cases, or 3 unordered pair-partitions each taken in both orders.

What it serves: the columns together survey the ways four objects can be ordered or grouped. Each column count is the multinomial coefficient 4!/(k1!…km!) for the given block sizes, restricted to the half-lists in columns 1 and 2. The previous page contains English notes on knots, citing Riedl and 's Gravesande. So the sheet may belong to a note on combinations of strands, but the page itself states no purpose.

The hand and the English-language context make it uncertain whether this sheet is by Gauss himself or a note kept among his papers.
errors: Column 1: the second entry 'acbd' is struck out and the list restarts at 'abcd'. This is a corrected false start, not a mathematical error.
Columns 1 and 2 are incomplete. Only arrangements whose first element is a or b are listed (12 of 24 and 6 of 12). This is probably intentional or abandoned, not an error.

Column 2: 'b.dc.a' writes the pair as dc rather than cd. As an unordered pair this is equivalent, but it breaks the alphabetical convention used elsewhere. If the column were instead meant as the 6 partitions of type {2,1,1}, the pair ab would be missing and cd duplicated. The ordered reading avoids that inconsistency.

results.what: Systematic lexicographic enumeration of permutations and ordered set-groupings of four letters (types 1+1+1+1, 1+2+1, 1+3, 2+2)
results.modern_name: Enumeration of permutations / ordered set partitions; multinomial coefficients
results.usually_credited_to: Classical combinatorics (Pascal, Leibniz 'De arte combinatoria' 1666, Jakob Bernoulli 'Ars Conjectandi' 1713, Hindenburg school)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary listing of arrangements of four symbols, with no theorem or method beyond standard 17th–18th century combinatorics. Authorship by Gauss is itself uncertain.

checkable.asserts: Permutations of abcd starting with a or b number 12 (column 1 count)
Ordered 1+2+1 arrangements with unordered middle pair number 12; column 2 lists half (6)
Ordered splittings into two pairs number 6 (column 4)
Total permutations of four letters, of which column 1 lists the 12 beginning with a or b
